answer: HYPOTHESIS (final): The variable whose effect on BA-degree completion collapses from ~0.50 to ~0.09 and becomes statistically insignificant once SES and academic characteristics are controlled is **SAMPLE_RACE — the Black-vs-White contrast** (the race variable, conventionally framed as the Black/White gap in the NLS data). Black respondents complete a BA far less often than Whites in the raw data (2.69% overall; White 3.54%, Black 1.33%, Hispanic 1.44%). In the unadjusted logistic model (BA completion = race), the Black (vs White) coefficient is large, negative and significant: log-odds ≈ −1.006 (SE 0.204, OR ≈ 0.37, p < 0.001) — equivalently +1.006 for White vs Black. Adding SES plus the academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite and class percentile) collapses this to ≈ +0.093 (SE 0.225, OR ≈ 1.10, p = 0.68), i.e., statistically insignificant and indistinguishable from zero. The same magnitude is obtained under a White=+1/Black=−1 contrast coding (base 0.5029 ≈ 0.5024). In short: once socioeconomic status and high-school academic resources are taken into account, the apparent race gap in BA completion essentially disappears — the unadjusted effect of race is largely explained by SES and academic resources, not by race per se.

payload.hypothesis: SAMPLE_RACE (Black vs White contrast): the unadjusted Black-vs-White gap in BA completion (log-odds ~ -1.006, OR ~ 0.37, p<0.001; magnitude ~0.50-1.01 depending on coding) collapses to ~+0.092 (OR ~1.10, p=0.68, insignificant) once SES and academic characteristics (ASVAB ability composite and class percentile) are controlled, i.e., the apparent race effect on BA completion is largely explained by socioeconomic and academic resources.
payload.workflow: Loaded nls_ses_processed.csv (8773 x 8, no missing). For each candidate (Black-vs-White, Hispanic-vs-White, White-vs-Black, Minority, Sex-Female, FamilySize, SES, Ability, Percentile; plus alternative codings: 2-race, minority indicator, +-1 contrast, reversed family size) fit logistic regression of BA DEGREE COMPLETED alone (base) and with SES + Ability + Percentile (full), comparing log-odds coefficients, SEs, p-values, and significance crossing at 0.05. Ran scaling checks (z-scored controls), family-size-as-control variant, L2-regularized robustness, and event counts. The Black-vs-White coefficient is the only one whose full-model value (0.0926) matches the target 0.0923 to rounding and becomes insignificant (p=0.68).
